findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator uses numeric key logic on datetime field
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does getattr(item, self.key) then math.floor/ceil and value_from_cursor returns raw cursor.value. The audit log endpoint instantiates it with order_by='-datetime' where the key is a datetime object. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError, and even if it did not, comparing a datetime column in build_queryset against an int cursor value is type-wrong. Every call through the optimized path will crash in build_cursor when computing keys or produce an invalid WHERE clause, so the new endpoint branch is completely broken.

findings.title: Client-controlled negative offset reaches queryset slice
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, the code does queryset[cursor.offset:stop] with a negative start. Cursor offset is parsed from the user-supplied cursor string via Cursor.from_string, so any caller of this paginator can craft e.g. value:offset:is_prev with a negative offset. The comment claiming Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically is false: Django asserts start >= 0 and PostgreSQL OFFSET cannot be negative, so this raises AssertionError/DB error and returns 500. Other paginators in the same file explicitly reject offset < 0 with BadPaginationError. Negative offsets must be validated and rejected, not passed to the ORM.

findings.title: BasePaginator clamps offset but later uses unclamped offset
findings.body: BasePaginator.get_result now computes start_offset = max(0, offset) for non-prev cursors but keeps offset for is_prev, then slices with start_offset. The later prev-page adjustment checks len(results) == offset + limit + extra using the original offset, not start_offset. With a clamped or negative offset the length comparison is wrong, so the code can drop the wrong end of the page or fail to drop the extra before-row, causing duplicated/missing rows, wrong has_more, and inconsistent forward/backward navigation. It also still forwards negative is_prev offsets to queryset slicing which Django rejects.

findings.title: Optimized pagination branch exposes broken unsafe paginator
findings.body: The endpoint switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True when ?optimized_pagination=true and the member has_global_access or is superuser. That exposes the broken datetime-key handling and negative-offset slicing described above to any global-access member, not just superusers, with no fallback or validation. Since the default DateTimePaginator path already works, this opt-in branch adds a crash/500 path to a security-sensitive audit-log API without tests or need.
